# Results — Study 901 (Profitable Small-Caps)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Asness-Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz-Pedersen (2018): the size premium lives in *profitable*
small caps; junky small caps drag it to zero** — put in tradable form: does a small-cap
**quality/profitability** ETF (CALF cash-cow, XSHQ small quality) beat plain small caps
(IWM/IJR) and SPY on **excess-of-cash Sharpe**, controlling for the size/value tilts and net
of costs? Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped). Fingerprint `3ec88092fc34`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes: CALF, XSHQ, IWM, IJR, SPY + BIL (cash leg) + `^IRX` (fallback) — public, no key |
| Window | tape 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-30 daily (as-of 2026-06-30); the Sharpe race is sliced to the **common window 2017-06-20 → 2026-06-30** (2,269 trading days) — CALF is the youngest contestant |
| Excess-of-cash | every Sharpe is **fund total return minus BIL total return**; a Sharpe race is a race of risk-adjusted *premia*, not cash-rate luck |
| Inference | annualised excess-Sharpe; **Newey-West HAC *t*** (10 daily lags) on the daily return difference and on the size/market regression; **paired circular-block bootstrap** Sharpe-difference CI |
| Costs | ER gap vs the plain baseline + 5 bps one-way on ~1 annual rebalance; the long-quality/short-plain isolation trade also pays 50 bps/yr borrow on the short leg |
| ERs (fund pages, 2026) | CALF 0.59 %, XSHQ 0.29 %, IWM 0.19 %, IJR 0.06 %, SPY 0.09 %, BIL 0.14 % |

> **Short-history / selection note (Signal axis).** CALF and XSHQ are **2017-vintage** ETFs:
> the profitable-small read has ~9 years of live tape, containing the 2020 COVID crash and the
> 2022 bear but no full pre-GFC cycle. These are also the *flagship survivors* of the
> small-cap-quality wave, not a random sample of every screen ever launched. Nine years is
> nine years — the stamp reflects it.

## The Sharpe race — profitable small caps did NOT beat plain small caps (common window)

Excess-of-cash, 2017-06-20 → 2026-06-30, n = 2,269 trading days:

| leg | what it is | ann. excess | ann. vol | **excess-Sharpe** | max DD |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **CALF** | profitable small (FCF cash cows) | +10.20 % | 25.97 % | **+0.393** | −49.2 % |
| **XSHQ** | profitable small (quality composite) | +8.99 % | 22.86 % | **+0.393** | −40.2 % |
| IWM | plain small (Russell 2000) | +10.11 % | 23.78 % | +0.425 | −43.0 % |
| IJR | plain small (S&P 600, mild earnings screen) | +10.21 % | 23.60 % | +0.433 | −46.1 % |
| **SPY** | large cap (yardstick) | +13.31 % | 18.68 % | **+0.712** | −33.9 % |

The two explicit "profitable small-cap" ETFs land at **Sharpe 0.39 — *below* both plain
small-cap indices (0.43)** and far below large-cap SPY (0.71). The quality screen did not
buy a higher risk-adjusted return; if anything it cost a hair. And no small-cap flavour,
cleaned or not, came close to SPY over this window.

## Bootstrap Sharpe CIs — everything small-cap straddles zero; only SPY clears it

Circular-block bootstrap (2,000 resamples), 95 % CI on each excess-Sharpe:

| leg | Sharpe | 95 % CI | P(Sharpe < 0) |
|---|--:|:--:|--:|
| CALF | +0.393 | [−0.234, +0.997] | 0.108 |
| XSHQ | +0.393 | [−0.209, +0.994] | 0.094 |
| IWM | +0.425 | [−0.209, +1.081] | 0.099 |
| IJR | +0.433 | [−0.204, +1.073] | 0.089 |
| **SPY** | **+0.712** | **[+0.109, +1.406]** | **0.012** |

Only the large-cap Sharpe is bootstrap-clear of zero. Every small-cap Sharpe — profitable or
plain — has a ~10 % chance of being negative on resampling.

## Head-to-head — the quality-vs-plain advantage is absent (paired bootstrap + HAC *t*)

Positive = the quality leg wins. `diff` is the **paired** Sharpe difference; the HAC *t* is on
the daily return difference:

| match | window (n) | Sharpe A vs B | **Sharpe diff** | 95 % CI | P(diff ≤ 0) | daily diff | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|:--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CALF vs IWM | 2017-06→2026-06 (2269) | +0.393 vs +0.425 | **−0.033** | [−0.323, +0.238] | 0.584 | +0.03 bps | +0.02 |
| CALF vs IJR | (2269) | +0.393 vs +0.433 | −0.040 | [−0.274, +0.170] | 0.643 | −0.00 bps | −0.00 |
| CALF vs SPY | (2269) | +0.393 vs +0.712 | −0.320 | [−0.760, +0.063] | 0.946 | −1.24 bps | −0.60 |
| XSHQ vs IWM | 2017-04→2026-06 (2316) | +0.396 vs +0.434 | −0.039 | [−0.286, +0.193] | 0.627 | −0.51 bps | −0.43 |
| XSHQ vs IJR | (2316) | +0.396 vs +0.438 | −0.043 | [−0.252, +0.135] | 0.671 | −0.52 bps | −0.54 |
| XSHQ vs SPY | (2316) | +0.396 vs +0.730 | −0.334 | [−0.724, +0.026] | 0.961 | −1.81 bps | −1.10 |

Every quality-minus-plain Sharpe difference is **negative**, its CI straddles zero, and the
HAC *t* on the daily difference is **≈ 0** — statistically no advantage in either direction.
Versus large caps the difference is a large, one-directional loss (P(diff ≤ 0) ≈ 0.95).

## Is there a "cleaned" alpha? — no (size/market beta decomposition)

Regress each quality leg's daily excess return on the small-cap factor (`x_IWM`) and the
market (`x_SPY`); the residual **alpha** is the part *not* explained by size or market beta:

| leg | alpha (%/yr) | HAC *t*(α) | β on IWM (size) | β on SPY (mkt) | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CALF | +0.93 | +0.27 | +1.059 (t = +33.1) | −0.108 (t = −2.8) | 0.816 |
| XSHQ | +0.73 | +0.26 | +0.887 (t = +36.6) | −0.063 (t = −1.6) | 0.773 |

CALF is a **β ≈ 1.06 loading on plain small caps** with **no distinguishable alpha**
(+0.9 %/yr at *t* = 0.27). The profitability screen did not add a cleaned premium on top of
small-cap beta — it *is* small-cap beta.

## Era cut — not era-robust (CALF vs IWM excess-Sharpe)

| era | window (n) | CALF Sharpe | IWM Sharpe | gap |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-2021 (incl. COVID) | 2017-06 → 2020-12 (891) | +0.364 | +0.499 | **−0.135** |
| 2021+ | 2021-01 → 2026-06 (1378) | +0.419 | +0.373 | **+0.045** |

The sign of the gap **flips** across the two halves (−0.135 then +0.045), and both magnitudes
are inside the bootstrap noise band — the opposite of the robust, pervasive advantage AFMP
document for the quality-cleaned size premium in the underlying stock cross-section.

## Tradability — costs push the already-absent edge further negative

**(a) Costed net Sharpe race** (charge the quality leg its ER gap vs IWM + 5 bps one-way on
one annual rebalance):

| leg | annual charge | Sharpe gross → net | IWM Sharpe | net gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CALF vs IWM | 0.45 %/yr | +0.393 → **+0.375** | +0.425 | −0.050 |
| XSHQ vs IWM | 0.15 %/yr | +0.396 → **+0.389** | +0.434 | −0.045 |

**(b) Long-quality / short-plain isolation trade** (dollar-neutral, 50 bps/yr borrow + 5 bps
one-way × ~2 rebalances/yr = 0.70 %/yr charge):

| trade | gross (%/yr) | HAC *t* | net (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CALF − IWM | +0.08 | +0.02 | **−0.62** | −0.18 |
| XSHQ − IWM | −1.28 | −0.43 | **−1.98** | −0.67 |

The isolation trade earns nothing gross and loses after costs. There is no positive edge for
costs to shrink — costs merely deepen a hole that starts at zero.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never market evidence)*

Deterministic world (`synthetic_world`, seed 901): quality = market + small-cap factor +
**planted edge**; plain = same systematic exposure + a zero-mean **junk** noise; the estimator
must recover the knob and the zero-edge null must NOT fire.

| planted edge | recovered Sharpe diff | 95 % CI | HAC *t*(daily diff) |
|--:|--:|:--:|--:|
| 0.0 (null) | −0.006 | [−0.301, +0.284] | −0.26 |
| 0.4 | **+0.425** | [+0.133, +0.718] | **+2.57** |

The null stays dark; a planted +0.4 Sharpe edge is recovered at +0.43 with a CI clear of zero
and HAC *t* = 2.6. The Sharpe-race machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape verdict (no
advantage, HAC *t* ≈ 0) is the genuine reading, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Put in tradable form, the "profitable small caps beat junky small caps"
  claim does **not** show up in the live ETFs. CALF and XSHQ post excess-Sharpe **0.39 —
  below** plain IWM/IJR (0.43) and far below SPY (0.71); every quality-minus-plain Sharpe
  difference is **negative** with a CI straddling zero and **HAC *t* ≈ 0**; the size/market
  decomposition leaves **no alpha** (+0.9 %/yr at *t* = 0.27; CALF is β ≈ 1.06 small-cap
  beta); and the tiny gap is **not era-robust** (sign flips −0.135 → +0.045). The machinery
  recovers a planted edge cleanly, so this is a true null, not a dead detector. The honest
  nuance: IJR (the mildly earnings-screened S&P 600) edges IWM by a whisker (0.433 vs 0.425),
  the faintest echo of the junk-control story — but it is noise-level and does not rescue the
  explicit quality ETFs.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no real edge to bank, and what *looks* like it could be
  one is entirely small-cap beta (β ≈ 1.06 on IWM). Costs make it worse, not investable: the
  costed net gap is −0.05 Sharpe, and the long-quality/short-plain isolation trade nets
  **−0.6 %/yr (CALF)** / **−2.0 %/yr (XSHQ)** after borrow and spreads. CALF's 0.59 % ER is a
  standing headwind against a 0.06–0.19 % plain-index baseline.
- **The real headline.** Over 2017–2026 **large caps (SPY) beat every small-cap flavour,
  cleaned or not**, on risk-adjusted return — the size premium, quality-screened or raw, was
  simply not paid in tradable ETF form this decade. AFMP's cross-sectional result may well
  hold in the underlying stock universe with a proper long-short QMJ overlay; a long-only
  profitable-small-cap ETF did not deliver it.
